findings.reason: the section must name the one order and its owner (the `CAUSES` tuple) so the attribution is deterministic and the done-when test pins it, instead of leaving two orders that disagree on a timeout log.
findings.text: §13 attributes each failed connection to "the first in §1's table that its log carries" and reports how many failures "also carried each later signature", but §1's table order (`CONNECTION_CLOSED`→`package_metadata`→`missing_directory`→`read_only_environment`→`CONNECT_TIMEOUT`→`server_discover`) is not the module's `CAUSES` order (`CONNECTION_CLOSED`→`CONNECT_TIMEOUT`→`package_metadata`→`missing_directory`→`read_only_environment`→`server_discover`): a log carrying both a `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` and the package-metadata stderr line is attributed to `package_metadata` by the plan's rule and to `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` by the natural `matched[0]` implementation at `reckon/mcp_census.py:245`, and the done-when case "counts once, under the earlier" cannot tell which order was used

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the census stays one public entry point, `census()`: §13 shrinks the interface (makes `directory_kind` private, the module's only other public function) while adding behaviour (one-cause attribution and the stale-directory skip), so depth grows as surface shrinks.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §13 fixes a failure's attribution as "the first in §1's table that its log carries", a second order beside the `CAUSES` tuple that owns the order and that the implementation will use; the two disagree for a `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` log.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1623, cli_options 351, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §13 adds no CLI option, no MCP view and no refusal family, and adds no public definition while retiring one (`directory_kind` becomes private), which the section states in its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §13 extends the landed `reckon/mcp_census.py` (its `_server_log_files` walk, its `CAUSES` signature table and its transcript count) rather than adding a second census; no other reader of Claude Code's `mcp-logs-*`/`claude-cli-nodejs` trees exists (grep finds none) and no other consumer of `STORAGE_SLOW`, and the section's new directory-mtime skip mirrors the transcript file-mtime skip the module already carries at `reckon/mcp_census.py:167`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §13 changes the existing census in place rather than placing a layer beside it, and `_echo_mcp_census` at `reckon/project_maintenance_commands.py:1055` stays the single reader of the report.
